DECISION: Very Confident', 'The clinical presentation—preceding viral-like illness (fever, rhinorrhea one week prior), followed by a facial rash with perioral sparing (“slapped-cheek” appearance) 4 days later, then a mildly pruritic, slightly raised rash on trunk and extremities—is highly characteristic of parvovirus B19 infection (fifth disease); the temporal sequence, distribution, and morphology align strongly with classic fifth disease, and no contradictory features (e.g., systemic toxicity, vesicles, purpura, mucosal ulcers, or atypical progression) are present.
